conceptZh: 蝦子身體彎彎，有長長的鬚
object: a tiny felt ninja and a stubborn bamboo fishing rod with a pink shrimp
morph: the fishing rod keeps misbehaving until the ninja lands the strokes of 蝦
creativeAngle: 布忍者想釣出字，釣竿不聽話，最後釣到一隻粉紅蝦。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蝦 (shrimp). Lead: a small black felt ninja with a floppy mask, certain nobody can see him even when he stands in the open. Moment 1 (0-1.7s): he tiptoes up and hides behind a thin reed, his whole body sticking out; the voice says 蝦 as he casts a bamboo rod that boomerangs and hooks his own hood. Moment 2 (1.7-3.4s): the rod has its own mind, flinging him upward; a pink stroke dangles from the line, then another; on the second 蝦 he finally lands the last stroke and 蝦 appears. Moment 3 (3.4-5.3s): the ninja hides behind the glyph with his feet visible; a big red-orange lobster with giant claws bursts from a bubble and the voice says 龍蝦 as the ninja freezes mid-tiptoe, eyes wide. Moment 4 (5.3-8s): glyph still; the ninja bows silently to the lobster, who waggles its claws. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蝦、蝦、龍蝦" (ㄒㄧㄚ、ㄒㄧㄚ、ㄌㄨㄥˊ ㄒㄧㄚ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蝦, drawn as saturated solid rose pink strokes on a pale mint background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.

conceptZh: 消防小隊為了澆熄小蝦尾巴上一點點小火苗，拚命猛催水管，結果消防車衝過頭、水管暴走把全隊噴飛，巨大水花落下來剛好排成「蝦」字，最後輕輕一滴水才把小火苗「噗」地熄掉，小蝦戴著消防帽跳出來。
object: a chunky red toy fire engine with a three-bear crew and a wild runaway hose, racing to put out one tiny candle-sized flame on a small pink cartoon shrimp's tail
morph: the over-powered hose blast launches a giant sheet of water; the splash freezes into rose-pink droplets that fall and lock into the strokes of 蝦, the 虫 column on the left and 叚 on the right, before a single gentle drop finishes the real job
creativeAngle: 改用「用力過頭」的套路：前一版是忍者釣蝦，這次是消防小隊為了一丁點小火苗動用全部馬力，衝過頭、輪子冒煙、水管反噬，水花砸下來反而排成蝦字，最後輕輕一滴才成功。字由水花落下形成，而不是物件直接變字；拍子每1.5–2秒換新動作，蝦子在說「蝦子」時戴消防帽跳出來，聲音與畫面完全對上。
promptEn:
An 8-second animated toy-world clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 蝦 (shrimp). Flat pale mint background, bright soft lighting, nothing busy behind. Lead: a chunky red toy fire engine with three round-headed toy bear firefighters, plus a fat yellow hose with a mind of its own. Goal: a small pink cartoon shrimp sits on a tiny toy grill at frame right with ONE candle-sized flame flickering on the tip of its tail, wiggling its whiskers, mildly annoyed.

Moment 1 (0-1.5s): the engine screeches in from the left, the captain bear stands on the roof and points dramatically at the tiny flame. All three bears gasp as if it were a skyscraper fire. The flame is the size of a birthday candle.

Moment 2 (1.5-3.3s): enormous wind-up. The bears crank a giant pump wheel with their whole bodies, the hose swells like a balloon, the engine rears up on its back wheels. The off-screen voice says the first 蝦 as the engine launches. It rockets straight past the grill, misses it completely, skids back with smoking wheels, and the overinflated hose whips loose and blasts all three bears off the roof in a cartoon tumble.

Moment 3 (3.3-5s): the BIG one. The wild hose fires a huge sheet of water straight up; the shrimp is flung high, spinning with a surprised face. The water sheet freezes mid-air, bursts into saturated rose-pink droplets, and they fall and lock down as the strokes of 蝦: the 虫 column slaps into place on the left, then 叚 on the right, each stroke landing with a soft plop. The second 蝦 is spoken as the final stroke snaps in and the glyph is complete, perfectly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins.

Moment 4 (5-8s): the glyph stays perfectly still. Below and to the right, well clear of the strokes, the dizzy captain bear holds the now-limp hose and gives it one gentle tap: a single drop falls on the tiny flame, which goes out with a little puff of steam. The pink shrimp pops up out of the grill wearing a tiny red firefighter helmet and flicks its curled tail happily; the voice says 蝦子 exactly as it pops up. The bears throw a tiny victory pose, one still wobbling, as the glyph holds clean for the full final 3 seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蝦、蝦、蝦子" (ㄒㄧㄚ、ㄒㄧㄚ、ㄒㄧㄚ ˙ㄗ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between utterances, then stops. No other speech, no music louder than the voice, no loud startling sounds. The only on-screen text is the single glyph 蝦 in solid rose pink on the pale mint background, uncropped, never touched or covered by characters. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading. Cartoon bonks only, nobody hurt.
